title: Vision
description:
What a `Token` can see, and what it carries to see by.

Vision has three independent parts. `enabled` decides whether the token sees at all — a
token without it contributes nothing to what the players are shown. `light` is a light source
the token carries, illuminating the map for everyone. `dark` is darkvision: the ability to
see without light, which reveals the map to this token alone.

The distinction matters on a dark map — a dwarf with darkvision sees the corridor, but the
human beside them sees only as far as their own torch reaches.

- SeeAlso: `Token`, `Light`, `Map/lineOfSight`

id.description:
The unique identifier for this vision configuration.

A UUID string generated when the object is created. Embedded objects have no primary key,
so this is indexed instead.

enabled.description:
Whether the token sees at all.

With this off the token is blind for line-of-sight purposes and reveals nothing.

light.description:
Whether the token carries a light source.

- SeeAlso: `Light`

lightRadiusMin.description: The radius of bright light the token emits, in grid units.

lightRadiusMax.description: The radius of dim light the token emits, in grid units.

lightColor.description:
The color of the light the token emits, as an RGB string.

## Examples
- `"#ffffff"`

lightOpacity.description: How strongly the emitted light tints the map, from `0` to `1`.

dark.description:
Whether the token can see without light.

Darkvision reveals the map to this token only, rather than illuminating it for everyone.

darkRadiusMin.description: The inner radius of darkvision, in grid units.

darkRadiusMax.description:
The outer radius of darkvision, in grid units.

## Examples
- `60` — the usual darkvision range in feet
